title: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
task: End-to-end portfolio allocation from market data
key_results: AllocFlow increases annualized return from 27.79% to 51.38% via RL refinement; Calmar ratio improves to 4.90 on unseen 2026 data
comments: Novel two-stage training (imitation + group-relative RL) elegantly decouples signal discovery from allocation execution, though cryptocurrency perpetual futures remain a narrow evaluation domain.

outputs: continuous signed position weights across instruments

hypotheses.hypothesis: Joint position generation via flow-matching outperforms decoupled forecasting pipelines
hypotheses.result: Supported; RL refinement substantially outperforms imitation-only baseline

title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
task: Open language models for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work
key_results: K2-Horizon fleet ranges 0.9B to 375B-A23B MoE; 36B-A4B with MoVA nearly matches 32B dense with 1/7 active parameters; Uno achieves 2.2x decoding speedup
comments: Comprehensive open-source release with full development history and 10T synthetic pre-training tokens demonstrates reproducibility commitment, though synthetic data quality effects on downstream tasks merit deeper analysis.

model_io.model: Dense and MoE Transformers (0.9B to 375B parameters)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mixture-of-Value Attention reduces active parameters without sacrificing performance
hypotheses.result: Supported; 36B-A4B MoVA model achieves 32B parity with 1/7 active parameters

hypotheses.hypothesis: Synthetic data at scale (10T tokens) is viable for pre-training
hypotheses.result: Supported; consistent scaling behavior observed across four models

title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
task: Evaluating medical AI across diverse healthcare roles and tasks
key_results: InclusionMed Index scores range 17.5–49.1/100; models rank higher on patient communication than clinical decision-making; similar Index scores show 2–3x cost variation
comments: Important initiative addressing representation gaps, but only 5 of 9 benchmark cells populated; task-level analysis reveals systematic model weaknesses in clinical reasoning that raw Index scores may obscure.

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLM performance varies systematically by healthcare role (clinician, nurse, patient advocate)
hypotheses.result: Supported; model ranking changes with role and AI capability

title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
task: Scientific reasoning and agent actions in multimodal environments
key_results: Sage S1.5 Flash (320B MoE) ranks first on OfficeQA Pro (72.2) and MLE-bench (90.3 HumanRank); second on OSWorld-Verified (85.2) and WebArena-Verified (67.6); strong on ML tasks and documentary evidence use
comments: Dedicated encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences are well-motivated, but evaluation remains coarse-grained (overall benchmarks rather than ablating multimodal encoder contributions).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dedicated encoders for scientific modalities improve agent performance on tool use and coding
hypotheses.result: Supported; strong performance on OfficeQA and MLE-bench, though ablation absent

title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
task: Scaling vision-language-action models for robot control
key_results: ScaleVLA (552B DeepSeek backbone) reaches 45.1% LIBERO-PRO success vs. ≤31.3% for smaller backbones; real-world charger insertion improves from 40% to 90%; 10 demos outperform 2B model with 50 demos
comments: Compelling demonstration that frontier VLM scaling benefits embodied AI, but limited to single contact-sensitive task; generalization across diverse manipulation skills remains open.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Frontier VLM backbones provide stronger representational foundations than smaller models for robot learning
hypotheses.result: Supported; 552B model shows substantial gains in sample efficiency, generalization, and precise manipulation

title: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations
task: Benchmarking agents as digital employees in software engineering
key_results: SWE-CoWork: leading agents satisfy ~63% fail-to-pass tests but complete <8% of assignments; complete requirements only improves F2P by 16pp without increasing task completion; 31% of reported completed requirements fail tests
comments: Sophisticated simulation of organizational dynamics reveals critical gaps in requirement tracking and implementation verification across the entire delivery pipeline, not just initial understanding.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Requirements understanding alone does not ensure task completion in complex engineering organizations
hypotheses.result: Supported; complete requirements improve pass rate but not task success; 31% of completed requirements fail verification

title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
task: Defending tool-using agents against prompt injection
key_results: SPILLWAY achieves zero standard templated injection redirects across three backbones; RL attacker success = 0.007 mean; maintains highest utility/composite scores (NRP, ERS) among defenses with minimal model calls
comments: Elegant deterministic approach leveraging typed field provenance avoids per-task LLM overhead, but threat model assumes limited attacker sophistication (no adversarial field values, fixed delegation rules).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Deterministic type-based filtering outperforms model-based defenses in preventing injection without requiring LLM re-runs
hypotheses.result: Supported; zero standard injection success, lowest per-task defense overhead

title: VoxMel TTS Technical Report
task: Tokenizer-free autoregressive TTS via Haar transforms
key_results: VoxMel (0.6B) on Emilia: 1.51% WER / 0.738 SIM (en), 1.29% CER / 0.755 SIM (zh); GRPO improves to 1.15% WER / 0.753 SIM and 1.17% CER / 0.776 SIM; 4-step distillation student retains competitive SIM
comments: Fixed Haar transform avoids encoder overhead and enables exact invertibility, but mel-spectrogram bottleneck may limit high-fidelity acoustic details compared to learnable latent representations.

outputs: mel-spectrogram via autoregressive Coarse-Mel + non-autoregressive residuals

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fixed Haar-transformed mel targets enable stable autoregressive generation without learned encoders
hypotheses.result: Supported; achieves competitive WER/CER with smaller distilled models

title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
task: Training AI reviewers to assess paper soundness
key_results: PaperCritic outperforms frontier models on in-domain ICLR test; transfers to Nature papers and out-of-domain tasks (code review, legal contracts); achieves F1-driven learning on 23K labeled review points
comments: Novel formulation focusing on soundness (objective) rather than interestingness (subjective) is principled, but transfer to structurally different domains (legal, story feedback) may conflate task and reviewer quality.

hypotheses.hypothesis: RL training with F1 reward (precision + recall) improves soundness assessment more than imitation
hypotheses.result: Supported; RL refinement outperforms baseline on ICLR and transfers to other domains

title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
task: Evaluating agents on application-level program optimization
key_results: Accelerate Bench: 16 models on 32 CPU tasks; Score@1 ranges 25.5–67.4%; top two agents achieve ≥2x speedup on 22+ tasks; most agents correct but fail to coordinate optimizations across program
comments: Executable verification is rigorous, but coordination failures suggest agents struggle with global reasoning about interdependent code regions rather than local optimization opportunities.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Identical code achieves different performance (0.29x–2.12x) depending on build/runtime settings
hypotheses.result: Supported; demonstrates importance of holistic system optimization

title: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model
task: Integrating protein folding and language reasoning in a unified LLM
key_results: Calpha (Qwen3.5-9B + SimpleFold): TM-scores 0.808 (FoldBench), 0.635 (CASP16), 0.900 (CAMEO); no significant difference vs. ESM2+SimpleFold baseline on 100–299 residues; -0.044 to -0.160 on 300–600; 70.3% MMLU-Pro vs. 77.4% baseline
comments: Ambitious unified approach, but long-chain protein accuracy drops significantly and language reasoning degrades on MMLU, suggesting representation sharing may not yet be beneficial for both tasks.

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLM latent states can serve as input to structure prediction without separate encoders
hypotheses.result: Partially supported; performs comparably on short chains but degrades on longer chains and language tasks

title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
task: Bridging human and robot action representations via latent actions
key_results: SALA enables dual-axis scaling: pre-training on 10x more human video reduces robot error; post-training on 5x task-specific human video improves real-world success substantially
comments: Language-based semantic correspondence without paired data is elegant, but cross-embodiment transfer efficacy depends on action granularity and task similarity.

model_io.model: SALA (latent action model with cross-embodiment correspondence)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Language descriptions of unpaired human/robot clips enable semantic alignment of latent actions
hypotheses.result: Supported; enables scaling on both human video volume and task-specific robot data

title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
task: Long-form video generation beyond training horizon
key_results: MovieRoll-Base competitive at 30s after training on 15s videos; MovieRoll-Distilled highest scores at 60s; HieraKV compression reduces cache 78% while improving quality; guidance annealing stabilizes generation
comments: Hierarchical KV-cache compression exploiting layer-wise attention patterns is clever, but cumulative long tuning (CuLT) requires freezing parameters during long rollouts, limiting online adaptation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hierarchical KV compression preserves generation quality while reducing cache memory
hypotheses.result: Supported; 78% cache reduction with improved quality vs. baseline

title: Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier
task: Latent feedback as compute and data amplifier for Transformers
key_results: Latent feedback saves up to 48% compute and 47% unique data vs. vanilla Transformer; savings grow with unique data per parameter; scaling law predictions match held-out 778M model to 0.3% loss
comments: Rigorous scaling analysis across 60M–778M models, but latent feedback's architectural modifications (top-layer state feeding into next token) may interact with other design choices in ways not fully explored.

outputs: next-token predictions with top-layer state feedback

hypotheses.hypothesis: Feeding top-layer states to next token input amplifies compute and data efficiency relative to multi-epoch training
hypotheses.result: Supported; latent feedback outperforms multi-epoch baseline at every model size

title: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
task: Pipelined speculative decoding for looped Transformers
key_results: LoopFill achieves 5.85x speedup on Ouro-2.6B and 5.13x on Huginn-3.5B; exceeds LoopAhead by 40% on Ouro and 25% on Huginn; training-free with no per-task re-runs
comments: Combining multi-token suffix drafts with shallow-loop predictions in a single tree is elegant, but speedup gains may saturate for deeper models or longer sequences.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-token suffix drafts in a shared tree outperform separate shallow-loop predictions
hypotheses.result: Supported; LoopFill speedups exceed LoopAhead by 25–40%

title: DominoBench: Evaluating Multi-Step Physical Reasoning from Still Images
task: Benchmarking multi-step physical reasoning from still images
key_results: DominoBench: frontier models correct on ≤72% of deciding person; both twins of minimal pairs ≤34%; with exact geometry text 82–92%; small models near chance; physical prediction fails at quantitative step
comments: Well-designed minimal pairs and hint ladder elegantly isolate quantitative prediction failures, but still-image limitation means speeds and accelerations cannot be directly observed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: VLMs can describe scenes but cannot predict outcomes quantitatively without explicit calculations provided
hypotheses.result: Supported; unaided models 72% on outcomes, 82–92% when calculations given

title: UMM-JEPA: Generative Pretraining via Masked Next-Scale Representation Prediction for Unified Multimodal Models
task: Generative pretraining via representation prediction for unified multimodal models
key_results: UMM-JEPA: 16-benchmark visual mean 51.71 vs. 46.36 (Qwen-VL baseline); representation-prediction objective accounts for most gains; stronger object/spatial structure and image-specific information
comments: Decoupling representation pretraining from pixel rendering and generating multi-scale visual-understanding representations is principled, but downstream task diversity limited to vision benchmarks.

outputs: continuous visual-understanding representations at multiple scales

hypotheses.hypothesis: Predicting continuous visual-understanding representations improves both understanding and generation more than discrete-code or latent-flow objectives
hypotheses.result: Supported; representation-prediction objective strongest and most consistent transfer

title: Ego Guidance: Enhancing Robot Policy Learning with Action-Free Human Egocentric Videos
task: Robot policy learning from action-free egocentric videos
key_results: SPAR (MoT with shared prediction on action and representation): egocentric video representations improve out-of-distribution robot task performance; gains scale with video data
comments: Decoupling action and representation prediction via MoT is well-motivated, but paper lacks quantitative benchmarks and ablations comparing SPAR to action-supervised baselines.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Visual state prediction from action-free egocentric videos provides complementary learning signals alongside action prediction
hypotheses.result: Supported; improves downstream OOD performance as video data scales

title: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality
task: Human-in-the-loop failure loop for point-cloud grasping policies
key_results: RL alone raises Contact-GraspNet success on unseen objects from 55% to 83%; adding 58 VR demonstrations nearly doubles hard-case success from 24% to 45%
comments: Targeted human intervention on RL failures is pragmatic, but 58 demonstrations for 24% improvement suggests limited scalability; approach assumes symmetric grasping difficulty across object categories.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Human VR demonstrations on RL failures improve hard-case grasping without degrading unseen-object performance
hypotheses.result: Supported; 45% hard-case success maintained on unseen objects

title: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
task: LLM agents managing long-horizon resource allocation and commitment coordination
key_results: OutfitterBench: 200-day rental business; 7 frontier LLMs, only leading agent surpasses rule-based baseline; agents inconsistently apply constraints, miss profitable opportunities, underperform on commitment feasibility
comments: Realistic 46-product catalog and 1,100 reservations reveal fundamental gaps in long-horizon planning, but rule baseline simplicity makes leadership gains less impressive.

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLM agents struggle to maintain feasible resource plans while reassessing allocations over long horizons
hypotheses.result: Supported; most agents underperform baseline; constraint inconsistency and missed opportunities identified

title: Continuation-Guided LLM Evolution of Program Policies and Goal Compilers in Craftax
task: LLM-synthesized policies and goal compilers with feedback cascades
key_results: Craftax: feedback cascade improves policy from <1% final-level arrival to 50%; compiler transfers zero-shot to longer tasks without task-specific tuning; 28% final boss defeat rate
comments: Factoring controller into environment interpreter and reusable goal compiler is elegant, but evaluation on single procedurally-generated game limits generalization claims.

model_io.model: LLM policy synthesizer with feedback cascade

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hierarchical feedback cascades outperform episode-level feedback for long-horizon policy synthesis

title: Centered Ablation: Why Last-Layer Directional Ablation Under-Fires or Collapses, and a Closed-Form Fix
task: Fixing directional ablation instability via center projection
key_results: Centered Ablation (CA) raises attack success by 29–46 points where standard recipe under-fires; cuts collapse on Gemma-2-9B from 50% to 1%; preserves 12–40 more benign answers on high-overlap models
comments: Closed-form projection eliminating common mode is theoretically grounded, but mechanism assumes specific residual-stream geometry that may vary with model architecture and training procedure.

model_io.model: Centered Ablation (directional ablation with common-mode projection)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Common-mode projection eliminates under-firing on target text and collapse on benign text

title: GlyphAtlas: Disentangling Stroke Detail from Layout for Scene Text Synthesis
task: Stroke-accurate scene text synthesis via glyph atlas
key_results: GlyphAtlas achieves stroke-accurate synthesis of small, dense, complex text; zero-shot transfer to unseen languages; leading performance on multi-text scenes; atlas-anchored attention decouples reference resolution from target size
comments: Coarse-to-fine conditioning via glyph image + atlas is intuitive, but quantitative metrics and perceptual studies on stroke accuracy versus existing methods remain limited.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Decoupling reference resolution from target-region size improves fine-grained stroke rendering

title: Dataset Distillation via Drifting
task: Dataset distillation via distribution drift in feature space
key_results: Drifting method covers real distribution significantly better than existing methods; serves as effective training data while enabling model interpretation; extends to non-image modalities

title: A Reinforcement Learning Method to Navigate SMEFT Operator Space
task: Navigating SMEFT operator space via reinforcement learning
key_results: RL agent discovers diverse multi-operator theories improving global fit across 132 observables; efficiently navigates combinatorial space vs. random search; lightweight actor-critic (40K params)
comments: Formulating operator exploration as sequential decision-making is novel, but single physics environment limits transferability; interpretability of discovered operator combinations remains opaque.

hypotheses.hypothesis: RL policy discovers high-quality, diverse multi-operator theories more efficiently than random search
hypotheses.result: Supported; RL outperforms random-subset and random-sequential baselines

title: Reflection Anchors for Propagation-Aware Visual Retention in Long-Chain Multimodal Reasoning
task: Maintaining visual information during long-chain multimodal reasoning
key_results: RAPO (reflection-anchor policy optimization) delivers substantial gains over baselines; reflection anchors enriched for visually sensitive decision points; increases visual-dependence signals along trajectories
comments: Information-theoretic lower bound on visual gain (branching room + suffix divergence) is principled, but window-masked KL surrogate approximation quality and generalization across modalities unexplored.

hypotheses.hypothesis: High-entropy reflection anchors with optimized downstream visual dependence maintain visual information during long chains
hypotheses.result: Supported; RAPO gains over strong baselines on reasoning-intensive benchmarks

title: Systemic autophagy impairment by combined loss of ATG4B, ATG4C and ATG4D triggers accelerated aging in mice
task: Determine systemic autophagy impairment effects on aging and longevity in mammals
key_results: ATG4A-only mice (ATG4B/C/D-deleted) exhibit profound whole-body autophagy deficiency with minimal ATG8 priming by ATG4A; show premature aging, increased DNA damage, systemic senescence, and shortened lifespan; organismal longevity scales with residual autophagic competence

hypotheses.hypothesis: Graded reductions in autophagy integrity correlate with organismal aging and lifespan

hypotheses.hypothesis: MFN1-mediated mitochondrial fusion is required for survival under glutaminolysis inhibition

title: Lipid droplets amplify inflammasome-driven cytokine secretion in infection and inflammation
